correctness.rationale: Writing \(A=\pi(kn)\), \(B=\pi((k+1)n)\), and \(d=B-A\) gives \(d\le\lceil n/2\rceil\) because the interval lies above \(2\). For \(x=kn\ge17\), Rosser--Schoenfeld gives \(A>x/\log x\). The elementary inequality \(\log x<x^{2/5}\) for \(x\ge17\) implies \((x/\log x)\log(x/\log x)>3x/5\), hence \(A\log A>3kn/5\ge k\lceil n/2\rceil\ge kd\). Thus \(k\log(B/A)<kd/A<\log A\), so \(B^k<A^{k+1}\). The seventeen pairs with \(kn<17\) are checked exactly. The packaged verifier reconstructs all small cases and stress-tests the argument over \(n\le2000\).

value.rationale: The result proves an explicit conjecture in a paper devoted to sixty open problems on combinatorial properties of primes. It is global in both \(n\) and \(k\) and replaces numerical evidence with a short structural argument using parity and a standard explicit \(\pi(x)\) lower bound. This is a complete conjecture resolution, not a finite extension or arbitrary parameter slice.
